newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds trapped, upside limited to 111-16.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds trapped, upside limited to 111-16.

text.p: September T-bond futures will be held in a broad range in the near term with 111-16 likely to be the upside limit on Tuesday, technical analysts said.

The market is nervous this week with fundamental factors taking precedence. The Federal Open Market Committee will begin its two-day policy meeting later in the session and key U.S. data are due this week, including the June employment report on Thursday.

"T-bonds are becoming marginally oversold and selling pressure is easing slightly. I suspect the worst of the fall has probably been see but I'm not looking for a recovery yet," said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst near Cambridge.
"The (upside) is likely to be inhibited by 111-16, that is the most one could look for," she said.
To the downside, Gifford said there was good support from Monday's low at 110-23 down to 110-12. On daily charts 110-12 marked the lows on June 10 and 12.
At 1002 GMT, September T-bond futures were at 111-02 in automated trade, unchanged from Monday's Chicago settlement.
Adrian Sells, director of Crane Investment Analysis in London, said T-bonds had a bad day on Monday. Prices slumped after a robust Chicago Purchasing Managers report.
"T-bonds had a bad day on Monday. But we rejected the lows at 110-23 fairly well and managed to close off them. So it was not as devastating as it might appear," he said.
The contract was in a big range between 110-08 and 111-24 and would churn around within it, he said.
"Tightening the range up is rather difficult because the market is vulnerable to being quite volatile and whippy," Sells said.
He said T-bonds would eventually try and base out but short-term there was the potential for some more (downside) pressure while the contract remained below 111-24.
At the short end, December Eurodollars were at 93.895, down 0.005 on the day.
